html:
Kenneth Kaunda was the first president of Zambia, leading it from independence on 24 October 1964 until 1991.

A teacher and son of a Malawian missionary, he led the United National Independence Party in the struggle against the Federation. As president he preached a philosophy he called Humanism, took control of the copper mines and made Zambia a one-party state in 1972.

He gave bases and shelter to liberation movements from Rhodesia, Namibia, Angola and South Africa, at a heavy cost to his country, which built the TAZARA railway to avoid white-ruled routes. When copper prices fell, the economy collapsed. He accepted multiparty elections and his defeat in the election of 1991, and later campaigned against AIDS.
sum: Kenneth Kaunda was the first president of Zambia, leading it from independence on 24 October 1964 until 1991.
